threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Word document engine exposing Rust byte APIs, a native CLI, PyO3/Python APIs and CLI, wasm-bindgen byte APIs and a Node CLI. It reads DOCX/OOXML, Markdown and supported legacy DOC inputs; compares, inspects, edits, resolves revisions, validates/repairs, scrubs and renders documents. Explicitly authorized host adapters publish resulting documents, reports, PDFs and PNGs. A Python MCP adapter serves document tools over stdio under a caller-selected directory capability. Native self-update and maintainer release publication are separate privileged workflows. The independent architecture reviewer reported current HEAD 41019ae16a6123f0273af0ca997901c85437be12; the scan-directory basename was not treated as its revision. Evidence: README.md:12-16,29-42; src/lib.rs:15-35,163-165; jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:42-49; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; src/update.rs:186-210.
assets: Confidential document bytes and extracted text, including paragraphs, comments, revisions, metadata, embedded images/fonts and relationship targets; generated clean/redline DOCX, rendered PDF/PNG and edit/audit reports. MCP intentionally returns text through read tools and page text through rendering, while document/image bytes are published as files. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:132-150,185-217,229-255; docs/adoption/mcp.md:69-73.

Integrity of edited documents, source snapshots and revision attribution. SHA-256 protects optional edit-plan snapshot binding; paragraph/text anchors and plan preparation protect edit applicability. Author strings are supplied document metadata, not authenticated identities. Evidence: src/inspect.rs:273-277; src/edit.rs:1744-1761,2073-2105; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:258-276.

Filesystem authority granted to the MCP server: explicit input reads and output publication beneath resolved --root, defaulting to startup working directory. The persistent native OutputRoot holds a cap-std directory handle. This is distinct from ambient filesystem authority used by CLI adapters and renderer font/cache operations. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1277; src/publication.rs:146-199,203-225.

Renderer resources outside explicit document paths: installed font files, Word cloud fonts and a persistent font-index TSV containing font source paths, file stamps and directory stamps. Default index location is the parent of Jubarte's font directory plus font-index.tsv, not a child of fonts/. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2258-2315,2633-2652,3090-3106,3154-3169,3192-3227.

Process memory, CPU and availability across native, Python and WASM callers. Default package admission allows 64 MiB compressed and per part, 256 MiB inflated, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison uses 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB inflated with the same entry/depth limits. XML limits default to 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte attribute names, 64 MiB values and 128 MiB start tags. These are configured objectives, with actual enforcement findings recorded separately. Evidence: src/admission.rs:63-100; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:49-57.

Installed native executable and the trusted release channel; release archives, SHA256SUMS.txt, optional signing-key material, GitHub release write authority and registry publication authority. Current updater trust configuration has no release public keys and no first-signed-release version. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:235-275,278-308,356-369; scripts/release.sh:72-84,105,375-380.
trustBoundaries: Untrusted document producer -> host process -> package admission and parsers. The host supplies bytes; admission implements archive size/count/inflation and structure controls before consumers parse input, including the shared ZIP structural pass. No disk extraction or external relationship fetching is part of admission. Public parse_xdocument deliberately does not enforce input policy; checked variants validate before DOM construction. Enforcement defects found in this audit remain separate from these intended controls. Evidence: src/admission.rs:13-28,397-407,439-470; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:85-135.

Document/edit-plan producer -> edit transaction -> transformed package bytes. Plans have schema checks, optional source_sha256 verification, exact-anchor failure modes and signed/macro-bearing source refusal; apply_plan returns prepared results rather than publishing files. Snapshot hashing authenticates neither author nor caller. Evidence: src/edit.rs:1740-1761,2073-2105; src/inspect.rs:273-277.

MCP client/model -> stdio server -> explicit root-relative input reads. Startup resolves --root or current working directory, opens one native OutputRoot and passes lexical relative names to read. Python resolution is an early diagnostic; actual confinement belongs to held cap-std directory capability. Tools do not establish independent users/tenants. Gemini extension starts uvx --from jubarte-redlines[mcp] jubarte-mcp --root ${workspacePath}, giving the same capability rooted at the host-selected workspace. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-89,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1262; src/publication.rs:146-165; gemini-extension.json:5-8.

MCP client/model -> brokered publication under the same held root. docx_edit derives out_dir/clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff and report.json, optionally redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png; docx_render derives out_dir/page-NN.png and render.pdf; compare/accept/reject use caller-selected output names. OutputRoot validates portable relative names, capability directories and output symlinks, stages/verifies files, and atomically installs each without clobber unless overwrite=true. Atomicity is per file; errors report committed files. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:101-112,185-217,229-277,285-298; src/publication.rs:83-143,168-199,228-273,431-482,535-570.

MCP registration/annotations -> external host approval policy. read_only_hint and destructive_hint are hints, not server-side caller authentication or approval enforcement. Host chooses approval policy; admitted calls can request overwrite=true and share a root. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,152-160,220-228; docs/adoption/mcp.md:39-41,168-169.

Native CLI operator -> ambient local output paths. publish_paths holds selected parent directory handles and stages verified bytes under sibling .jubarte-<UUID>.partial/bytes with private Unix permissions; typed edit publication rechecks input hash and output aliases/collisions. Partial commits may remain after a later error. This grants ambient access rather than MCP root confinement. Evidence: src/publication.rs:203-225,431-505,535-570; src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273,1642-1656,1764-1812.

Python/Node CLI operator -> ambient filesystem. Python _write uses Path.write_bytes and Node write uses fs.writeFileSync after adapter path/force checks; these do not inherit native publication merely from shared engine grammar. Python Document.read uses ambient read_bytes; in-memory operations return bytes. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:117-145; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:116-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79,106-111.

Document-selected font family -> native renderer -> ambient font stores using std::fs, outside MCP OutputRoot. Own-font directory precedence: nonempty JUBARTE_FONT_DIR, otherwise macOS HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts; other Unix XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts (HOME required); Windows APPDATA/jubarte/fonts. System/Word discovery separately uses /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental, /Library/Fonts, /Applications/Microsoft Word.app/Contents/Resources/DFonts, /Library/Fonts/Microsoft, /System/Library/Fonts and HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>. Cloud family is one normal path component. Windows discovery uses WINDIR, else SystemRoot, else C:\Windows joined with Fonts, plus LOCALAPPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts. These resources feed font parser/shaper and rendered output, controlled by ambient OS permissions. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2230-2235,2258-2315,2324-2376,2460-2467,2633-2652,2814-2862.

Native renderer -> persistent ambient font-index state. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX empty/off disables; another value is complete path; absent value derives parent(user_font_dir())/font-index.tsv. Effective defaults: HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv on macOS, XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv on other Unix, APPDATA/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Windows. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides instead derive its parent/font-index.tsv. Reads reuse stamped source paths; writes create parent, write sibling font-index.tsv.<pid>.tmp then rename. No MCP-root control applies; OS permissions, index version/header, file/directory stamps are effective controls. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3095-3112,3154-3188,3213-3229.

JS caller -> WASM linear memory -> shared engine. WASM exports take byte arrays/JSON and return bytes/results, omit self-update, and cfg-exclude native publication. Node CLI separately supplies filesystem authority. WASM compare inherits roomier 2 GiB inflated comparison budget and documentation tells browser hosts to lower it. Evidence: jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:63-97; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-55,106-111.

Operator -> explicit native self-update -> GitHub release/archive/SHA256SUMS.txt -> executable swap. Fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines and OS/arch target select archive and member jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte (Windows jubarte.exe). macOS/Linux use tar.gz, Windows ZIP; extraction/swap delegated to self_update. Noninteractive requires --check or --yes before network lookup; interactive installation confirms. verify_binary rejects nonregular extracted binary. RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean checksum-only verification, matching staged-signing docs. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,186-210,212-257; Cargo.toml:137-148; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-45,57-87.

Maintainer/tag authority -> GitHub Actions builds -> release publication. v* tag triggers tag/version check and per-platform locked read-only builds; release job gets contents:write and same-run artifacts. Optional signing alone receives ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, decodes to RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN, signs dist archives, verifies committed keys/*.pub and deletes keys on exit. Checksums follow signing. GITHUB_TOKEN maps to GH_TOKEN for gh release create at GITHUB_REF_NAME in github.repository, notes.md and dist/*. Local release.sh additionally publishes registries and runs security-check.sh even when ordinary gates skipped. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-25,40-49,51-89,235-308,317-322,356-369; scripts/release.sh:72-84,105,375-380,654-678.

Developer benchmark worker -> ambient paths over stdin COMPARE basePath nextPath outPath -> std::fs reads/writes. It is a same-user speed harness, not a hosted network service; independently exposed deployment would require separate controls. Evidence: jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:5-20,29-69,91-99.
attackerCapabilities: A document producer controls container records, XML/relationships, text, revision/comment metadata, embedded media/fonts and legacy DOC bytes. This is a parser/resource boundary without proof of a public service. Input budgets/shared ZIP checks/checked XML are existing controls, not proof of complete DoS resistance. Evidence: SECURITY.md:33-80; src/admission.rs:13-28,63-100,439-470.

An MCP client/model chooses exposed tool arguments, relative paths, plans, output names and overwrite flags within root. It does not thereby control --root, environment/font-index settings, installed binary, signing keys or release credentials. All calls share root; no tenant identities established. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-160,220-228,373-381.

Untrusted returned text may influence a consuming model, but interpreting it as instructions/granting tools is an external host decision. MCP hints are metadata, not identity enforcement. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,132-150; docs/adoption/mcp.md:39-41.

Replacing release assets plus adjacent checksum differs from source/build/signing-key authority. Present updater does not have independent signature trust root. GitHub publication/transport compromise is an additional prerequisite, not granted by ordinary document input. Evidence: src/update.rs:44-48,198-210,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80.

Write access to shared output/font/cache state could influence a privileged consumer but must be established for a deployment. Publication mitigates races with held directories/staging/atomic installation; renderer cache has separate ambient authority. Evidence: src/publication.rs:431-482,535-570; src/convert/font.rs:3154-3188,3213-3229.
securityObjectives: Refuse malformed/ambiguous/over-budget documents before unrestricted package inflation/DOM work; preserve checked versus raw XML distinction. Use host CPU/memory limits rather than claiming comprehensive execution limits from admission. Findings record exceptions. Evidence: src/admission.rs:39-40,63-100,397-407,439-470; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:90-135; SECURITY.md:74-80.

Confine explicit MCP document I/O to startup root, preserve no-clobber unless overwrite=true, report partial commits/durability uncertainty. Do not mistake broker controls for process-wide sandboxing. Evidence: src/publication.rs:36-46,146-199,431-482,535-570; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108.

Bind edit plans to inspected bytes when source_sha256 supplied; refuse unsupported schema/stale snapshot/ambiguous anchors before publication. Author attribution is separate from authentication. Evidence: src/edit.rs:1744-1761,2073-2105; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1656,1781-1805.

Protect confidential document and derived output across returned text/artifacts/reports. Scrub/redaction are explicit transformations requiring dedicated review; successful conversion/validation does not establish confidentiality. Evidence: src/lib.rs:19-27; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:132-150,185-217,245-255.

Restrict executable replacement to deliberate updater, intended repository/platform/release and configured checksum/signature/regular-file policy. Keep checksum-only state explicit until keys compiled in. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,198-210,240-257.

Scope release credentials to consumers and bind artifacts to version/tag/build outputs. Signing keys, GitHub release credentials and registry tokens are distinct capabilities. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:40-49,89,235-308,317-322,356-369; scripts/release.sh:72-84,105,375-380.

Root SECURITY.md resolved by supplied helper covers engine/CLI/Python/WASM and is analysis data, not authority to expand task.

Documentation discrepancy: mcp_server.py:67-68 says tools only touch files under root; docs/adoption/mcp.md:61-75 describes root-confined operations. Actual explicit document I/O is confined, but renderer independently reads ambient font stores and reads/writes font index and temporary sibling outside --root. Both statements retained. No unauthorized disclosure/write impact established from discrepancy alone. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,185-188,234-236; src/convert/font.rs:2258-2315,2633-2652,3095-3106,3213-3229.

Signing is staged rather than active. docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:69-80 permits checksum-only until key committed; src/update.rs:44-48 contains empty keys/no first version. Read general signature explanation at docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-65 together with effective state.

MCP inspected startup is stdio-only. Host owns authentication/approval policy/process isolation/cwd and separation of server instances. No public HTTP service, tenant database or remote exposure established. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; docs/adoption/mcp.md:76,168-169.

Python/Node direct-write CLI helpers differ from native staged publication; shared parser parity does not establish filesystem atomicity/race parity. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111.
Benchmark stdin worker is developer-only ambient-path harness, not hosted service. Evidence: jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:5-20,29-69,91-99.

Legacy DOC uses distinct OLE/FIB/piece-table path, not DOCX admission; docs limit to main story and refuse old/encrypted/obfuscated formats. Findings add validated resource failures without assuming identical admission controls. Evidence: src/legacy_doc.rs:13-44,180-235.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with malformed WMF text records can exhaust host memory
findings.summary: A document author can embed short WMF records whose text counts borrow bytes from following records. Rendering repeatedly copies overlapping input into retained strings, expanding roughly 1 MiB of media into multiple GiB and potentially terminating the host process.

severity.rationale: High availability impact from small attacker-controlled document media; likelihood is medium because a victim must render the supplied DOCX. No remote service deployment is assumed; process limits reduce impact.
severity.changeConditions: Lower with effective per-job memory/CPU isolation; higher likelihood if exposed through an automatic untrusted document conversion service.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace establishes public rendering, attacker media dispatch, missing record-relative bounds and retained allocation; no runtime reproduction was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Embedded document media reaches metafile rendering
codeEvidence.explanation: The document controls the embedded relationship and package media bytes; collect_images forwards those bytes to decode_image.

codeEvidence.label: Image decoder invokes the WMF parser
codeEvidence.code:
fn decode_image(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Option<ImageKind> {
    if let Some((width, height, rgb, texts)) = metafile::render(&bytes) {
codeEvidence.explanation: WMF parsing precedes the ordinary image decoders, so raster image-library limits do not constrain its text expansion.

codeEvidence.label: Record size only controls cursor advancement
codeEvidence.explanation: This validates the declared record extent in the file but passes the whole data buffer to record handlers rather than a slice confined to that extent.

codeEvidence.label: Text reads cross into later WMF records
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker chooses n independently of size2. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT with n=65535 consumes the next 65535 bytes yet the loop advances only 14 bytes. TEXTOUT at lines 614-620 shares this whole-file bounds error.

codeEvidence.label: Decoded text is allocated and retained
codeEvidence.explanation: Each overlapping slice becomes an owned string retained in texts; nonzero extents and nonwhitespace record bytes satisfy the return checks.

rootCause.summary: collect_images resolves attacker-selected package media and decode_image dispatches placeable WMF bytes to raster_wmf. The loop checks each declared record size but EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT read their attacker-supplied text lengths against the entire media buffer. Advancing by the short declared size causes overlapping later bytes to be decoded and retained repeatedly in MetaText, without a cumulative expansion budget.

findings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler to its declared record slice, reject payloads/counts that exceed that slice, and enforce cumulative text/geometry/work budgets before allocation. Apply the same record confinement to EXTTEXTOUT, TEXTOUT, polygon and other sibling handlers.

counterEvidence: WMF canvas side is capped at 384 and record size arithmetic is checked; neither bounds retained strings.
InputLimits bounds compressed/inflated package bytes and XML depth, not WMF logical text.
An operator's process limits can contain impact; no production deployment was established.
limitations: No malicious file was constructed and no application code was executed.
validation.summary: Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.

dataflow.summary: Untrusted DOCX media -> collect_images -> decode_image -> metafile::render -> raster_wmf whole-buffer text slices -> owned MetaText strings retained in texts.
dataflow.source: Attacker-controlled WMF record sizes and text counts
dataflow.outcome: Host memory/CPU exhaustion, including potential native host termination or WASM memory trap.

impact.why: Multiple GiB of retained allocation from a small document can kill the host process.

likelihood.why: Requires document rendering and absence of sufficiently strict per-job process limits.

reachability.summary: Public Rust docx_to_pdf/render and their binding consumers process caller-supplied package media after package admission; no network exposure is required.
reachability.attacker: Author of an untrusted DOCX rendered by another user or host
reachability.outcome: Loss of availability in the rendering process.
preconditions: Referenced media is a placeable WMF with a nondegenerate canvas.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with a referenced placeable WMF containing many 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT records, count 65535, nonzero extents and sufficient trailing bytes; induce PDF/PNG rendering.

remediationTests: Small malformed EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT records must be rejected without reading following bytes.
Repeated short records must remain within deterministic cumulative allocation/work limits.
Verify valid WMF text still renders through public PDF/PNG APIs.

provenance.discoveredBy: baseline subagent; independently validated by parent

originalCandidates.originalEvidence: src/convert/metafile.rs 603-610 EXTTEXTOUT bounds text slice against whole data, not current record end off+size2; off advances size2 at690. Repeat 14-byte records (size=7 words, func0x0A32, y=x=opts=0,count=65535) followed by >=65535 bytes of padding. Each record copies next65535 bytes via ansi_text->String into texts Vec (431-440,692-700), yielding ~4GiB retained strings from ~1MiB WMF. No per-record or cumulative text bound; header canvas extents nonzero. decode_image (20248) calls render before image decode. Also polygon counts read across record boundary, amplifying CPU.

findings.title: Converting a small legacy DOC can exhaust host memory through reused text pieces
findings.summary: An author can reuse the same physical WordDocument text range in thousands of logical pieces. The legacy reader materializes one StoryChar per logical character without an expansion budget, allowing a roughly 1 MiB text stream plus a small piece table to demand tens of GiB before DOCX admission runs.

severity.rationale: High availability impact and medium likelihood: a victim must import an attacker-supplied legacy DOC. Parsing is public and enabled by the CLI, but remote deployment is not assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-job memory/CPU isolation reduces impact; automatic untrusted DOC import increases likelihood.

confidence.rationale: Independently traced public read/doc_to_docx and CLI entrypoints through independent CP/FC fields to per-character retained allocation. Physical bounds and monotonicity checks do not prevent reuse. No runtime reproduction.

codeEvidence.label: Public legacy reader forwards untrusted piece metadata
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker supplies both the FIB logical character count and piece-table entries. The public reader reaches text expansion before later style/table parsing.

codeEvidence.label: Logical character ranges and physical file offsets are independent
codeEvidence.explanation: Monotonic logical CP ranges can all carry the same valid physical FC; bytes need not be duplicated on disk.

codeEvidence.label: Every logical character creates retained output
codeEvidence.explanation: Iteration is controlled by the declared logical span, and the physical cursor resets for every piece. No cumulative logical character or output allocation budget is checked.

codeEvidence.label: StoryChar allocations accumulate across all pieces
codeEvidence.explanation: Each logical CP is retained with character, offsets and modifiers; repeated physical ranges therefore multiply allocation.

codeEvidence.label: CLI imports legacy DOC before package admission
codeEvidence.explanation: A normal convert operation automatically invokes the vulnerable reader for OLE input. Later DOCX admission cannot bound this earlier expansion.

rootCause.summary: The FIB and piece table independently provide total logical characters, logical CP ranges, and physical FC offsets. main_text checks monotonic coverage and each physical read, then expands every logical CP into an owned StoryChar. Reusing a valid physical text range across many logical pieces passes those checks while multiplying retained memory; no logical expansion budget precedes the loop.

findings.remediation: Enforce an explicit maximum logical story length and cumulative expanded bytes/work before iterating or allocating. Carry host InputLimits or equivalent legacy limits through all public DOC readers and CLI conversion; allow legitimate physical piece reuse only within that budget.

counterEvidence: Compound-file sector walks and numeric offsets use checked/bounded arithmetic; these bound physical reads, not logical reuse.
Main-story CP coverage must be continuous and increasing; the described pieces satisfy that condition.
Process memory/CPU limits are recommended by SECURITY.md and can contain the host impact.
limitations: No generated DOC or application execution; exact peak allocation and abort behavior were not measured.
validation.summary: Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.

dataflow.summary: Untrusted DOC -> CompoundFile/Fib/pieces -> main_text -> per-logical-CP StoryChar vector -> memory exhaustion.
dataflow.source: Attacker-controlled ccp_text, CP ranges and FC offsets
dataflow.outcome: CPU exhaustion and allocator failure/host process termination.

impact.why: Small input can demand tens of GiB of retained allocations.

likelihood.why: Requires legacy document import and insufficient process resource isolation.

reachability.summary: Public legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown and doc_to_docx accept caller bytes; CLI convert autodetects OLE and invokes doc_to_docx before DOCX limits.
reachability.attacker: Author of a legacy DOC processed by another user or host
reachability.entrypoint: Legacy DOC public reader and CLI convert
reachability.outcome: Loss of importer availability; no additional filesystem or network authority is required.

attackPath.summary: Supply an OLE DOC whose piece table repeats a physical text region under consecutive large CP ranges, then induce legacy read or conversion.

remediationTests: A compact valid compound file with repeated FC pieces and excessive logical CP coverage must be refused before expansion.
Boundary-sized permitted stories and legitimate reused text pieces should import successfully.
CLI conversion must apply the same logical expansion budget as direct library calls.

findings.title: Nested legacy DOC field results cause quadratic parser work
findings.summary: Importing a small DOC with repeated field-begin/separator pairs builds a deep stack of false field states. The reader rescans that stack for every input character, allowing hundreds of kilobytes to consume billions of checks and monopolize the conversion thread.

severity.rationale: High availability impact with medium likelihood because a victim must import an attacker-provided legacy document; no public service is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-job CPU deadlines or process isolation lower impact; automatic shared document import increases likelihood.

confidence.rationale: Independent source validation confirms unbounded state stack, full any() traversal on all-false states and public legacy-reader reachability. No benchmark executed.

codeEvidence.label: Every decoded character scans the field stack
codeEvidence.explanation: The document controls field markers. Alternating begin and separator leaves all existing stack entries false, forcing any() to traverse depth before every subsequent begin and pop.

codeEvidence.label: Legacy reader sends decoded characters to block parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The public read path invokes this algorithm on caller-supplied main-story text.

rootCause.summary: Story::blocks recomputes whether any active field is in its code using a linear scan for every StoryChar, while accepting arbitrary field nesting. False states accumulate from nested field-result separators, making total work quadratic without requiring any physical text aliasing.

findings.remediation: Maintain a constant-time active-code counter alongside the field stack and enforce a reasonable configurable nesting limit before pushing.

counterEvidence: Physical reads and offsets remain checked.
CLI timeout exists but defaults to None; direct library read has no deadline.
This requires victim legacy-DOC processing and is bounded externally by optional process limits.
limitations: No timing measurement or exploit file execution.
validation.summary: For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
